description: Task #92 minimal reproducer — leap-rust/leap-c divergence on random/groupby/slt_good_11.test when SELECT DISTINCT contains an output alias whose name shadows an underlying column and HAVING references that name. Root cause: leap-c's DISTINCT-wrapping re-entered sl_compile and double-applied apply_alias_substitution, which for alias-shadowing-column cases collapses the HAVING ref back to the base column (i.e. alias-in-HAVING becomes a no-op under DISTINCT for shadowing names). leap-rust only substituted once. Fix: when `distinct` is set, rewrite_core_with_alias_scope now applies alias_refs_in_expr twice to HAVING, mirroring leap-c's accidental behaviour and matching mainline SQLite result. Fixture cases are also integrated into phase6aj.json so they run under the regular rust/c regression harness.

cases.name: distinct-having-alias-shadows-column
cases.description: Reproducer drawn directly from slt_good_11.test line ~13219. Pre-fix leap-rust returned [[-81]]; post-fix returns [] matching leap-c and mainline SQLite.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE tab0 (col0 INTEGER, col1 INTEGER, col2 INTEGER);
SELECT DISTINCT -col1 AS col1 FROM tab0 GROUP BY col2, col1 HAVING NOT AVG(DISTINCT -col2) <= (+col1);

cases.name: distinct-having-base-col-wins
cases.description: Minimal variant — `HAVING x > 0` with alias `-x AS x` under DISTINCT must compare the BASE x (positive), not the aliased -x.

program.sql: SELECT DISTINCT -x AS x FROM t GROUP BY x HAVING x > 0 ORDER BY x;

cases.name: non-distinct-having-alias-still-wins
cases.description: Without DISTINCT, HAVING continues to resolve to the output alias. Confirms the DISTINCT-specific asymmetry.

program.sql: SELECT -x AS x FROM t GROUP BY x HAVING x > 0;

cases.name: distinct-having-non-shadowing-alias-unaffected
cases.description: When the alias name does NOT collide with a base column, the double-substitute is a no-op and HAVING still resolves to the alias expression.

program.sql: SELECT DISTINCT -x AS neg FROM t GROUP BY x HAVING neg < -1 ORDER BY neg;
